sasha: Heads up — after yesterday's kernel-routing tweak I'm seeing an uptick in per-GPU OOMs on long-context tails. Not huge, but reproducing locally with the same trace.

sasha: profile snapshot (light):
```
alloc_reserve: 12MB -> 4MB after route change
active_workspace: 580MB (peak)
kv_cache_hold: 220MB
decode_window: 128 -> 256 steps (some requests)
OOM at: workspace_alloc(604MB)
```

sasha: hypothesis: the route change favored smaller kernels so we reduced soft-reserve to squeeze latency, but that removed a safety buffer for spikey prefill+decode combos.

junaid: Hmm. I saw a related regression in CI perf dashboards — tail latency improved but mem pressure increased. Link: https://internal.redwood/perf/dashboards/memory-pulse?run=1765 :eyes:

junaid: Two knobs we can consider: (1) reserve decay rate (how quickly we release prefix/KV reserves) and (2) per-request soft cap (enforce earlier prefill demotion).

carmen: +1. Also worth checking allocator bin packing waste. If fragmentation jumped due to smaller kernels, the effective usable buffer could be much lower than raw free. I ran jemalloc-style metrics yesterday and saw free-chunk-count up 3x.

carmen: Quick thought experiment: keep reserve high for short-lived bursts (200ms) but aggressively decay if sustained low usage. That lets us handle prefill spikes without permanently losing density.

junaid: Agreed. We should try a pulse-style reserve: on incoming prefill, grant a temporary delta reserve that decays exponentially with half-life T. Tune T ~ 150-300ms. Also add a global inhibitor if free fragmentation > 40% to cap pulse size.

sasha: I can prototype: add a per-GPU ephemeral reserve queue + kernel-routing hook to request extra soft-reserve when switching to small-kernel path. That ensures decode-prefill combos won't race the recycler.

carmen: If we do that, we need metrics: pulse_grants, pulse_expirations, pulse_failed_due_to_frag, plus tail_OOM_count by request-type. I'll add them to the tracer.

perf-bot: New experiment created: memory/pulse-reserve-v1 (seed=42). 50 runs scheduled on dedicated-staging.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy queued for memory/pulse-reserve-v1 to staging cluster cluster-staging-7. ETA ~ 30m.

junaid: For the rollout, let's set conservative defaults: pulse_max=48MB, half_life=200ms, frag_gate=35%. Start with per-request soft-cap at 85% of effective workspace to leave room for KV decode.

sasha: I'll push a branch with the hook + simple in-memory pulse allocator. Will include a small repro script that simulates prefill+decode tails.

carmen: FYI we should also try toggling kernel selection thresholds: if kernel_choice==small && expected_decode_steps>200 then bias towards the larger kernel to reduce fragmentation. Might cost some latency but avoid OOMs.

junaid: Good call. We should A/B that as a routing policy: latency-first vs safety-first. Add rollout flags.

sasha: Copy. I'll post logs once staging runs finish. For now, anyone seen any other quick wins?

carmen: Maybe a cheap compaction pass triggered when free-chunk-count spikes and recent pulse_failed_due_to_frag > 0. Compaction is costly but rare.

junaid: Agree, but add guard: only allow compaction if node idle% > 50% for last 1s to avoid hurting throughput.

sasha: Great. Syncing up in 30m after canary. Thanks. :thumbsup:
